Tyler Toffoli has gone seven straight games without a point, and our numbers say it's mostly bad luck: about four expected goals of chances in that span with nothing to show. His shooting percentage this season is 9.8%, below where we'd expect a career scorer like him to settle. He has nine points in 19 games.

He's 34, a Stanley Cup winner with the Kings in 2014, an alternate captain, and one of the few veterans on a Sharks team that has lost seven of eight. Toffoli has been one of the voices talking publicly about frustration and buy-in in San Jose. Since Wennberg's injury he's playing more, up to about 15 minutes a night, often with Kiefer Sherwood and Mason Marchment.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins last season, mostly from even-strength offense, and his wins added this season rank 83rd of 504 skaters, so the goals he has scored have mattered. Our range projects 14 to 26 goals over a full season. The drought is the kind that ends with a two-goal night.
headline: Toffoli's drought is mostly bad luck
